finding: app.js:129 Success toast is shown for the whole batch without reading the refund response. api.js:34-38 returns the parsed body, and app.js:128 discards it. Only res.ok is checked (api.js:15). README.md:13 claims success is reported 'only after the server confirms it'. A batch endpoint taking an array of ids can answer 200/207 with per-id outcomes; none is read. The same code treats a 200/204 with an empty body as a failure (api.js:16-20, then app.js:133), so a refund that did succeed shows as 'not confirmed'. domain.js:28 Revenue stat re-applies a gold discount and sales tax to the server's order total. orderRevenueCents (domain.js:25-30) takes order.total, applies -10% for gold, then +8.25% tax. The refund confirm (app.js:122-123) uses the raw o.total, so the two screens disagree. The server sets and charges the amount; the client holds a second copy of the pricing rule. The summary also averages over every order, including pending and refunded ones that contribute 0 (domain.js:35). The requirement is inferred; no document says whether total is pre- or post-discount. With one paid and one pending order of 100.00, 'Average per order' shows about $48.71 rather than $100.00 for paid ones. If the rates change on the server, the dashboard goes silently wrong.

app.js:128 A new idempotency key on every click defeats the double-refund protection in exactly the ambiguous-failure case. api.js:32 says the key lets the server ignore a repeated request for the same attempt, and README line 8 says a repeated request must not refund twice. app.js:128 mints a fresh key per click. After a failure the catch at app.js:131-133 keeps state.selected, and the finally block re-enables the button. A network error (api.js:13), an invalid-JSON body (api.js:19) and a 5xx all land there, and the server may already have refunded. The guard against a retry is wording only. Traced. User refunds 3 orders. The server processes the refunds, but the response is lost or the proxy times out, so the user sees 'The refund was not confirmed. The server could not be reached.' The 3 rows are still ticked and 'Refund 3 orders' is enabled. The user clicks it again and confirms; the new UUID is a different key, so the server refunds the 3 orders a second time. The same happens if the refund endpoint answers 200/204 with an empty body: res.json() throws at api.js:17, a success is reported as a failure, and the retry pays twice.

app.js:72 Disabling the focused Next, Previous or Refund button drops keyboard focus to the page body. renderTable sets prev/next disabled (app.js:71-72) right after the click that moved the page. renderRefundButton (app.js:83) disables the refund button while refunding and again when the selection is cleared after the reload (app.js:98). Next becomes disabled, focus is lost and the next Tab starts again from the top of the document. Missing totals: normaliseOrder in domain.js accepts an order whose total is null or "" as a $0 order, because Number(null) and Number("") are both 0. Its comment says such records are dropped. This only matters if the API sends null totals, so I treated it as input-dependent.

app.js:128 A new idempotency key is generated on every click, so retrying a refund whose first response was lost sends a different key. The user confirms a refund and the server processes it, but the response is dropped (timeout or network error). refund() throws, and the message tells the user to retry. The retry gets a fresh UUID, so the server's Idempotency-Key dedup never matches and the customer is refunded twice. The key should be kept per attempt (per set of ids) and reused until the outcome is known. The README's claim that a repeated request does not refund twice only holds if the client reuses the key.
